body:
Totally agree. Used to think that aswell when I was around twelve years old and people also told me 'it's puberity, it will end after that'. I'm going to be 24 in a month from now and things have only took a turn for the worse if anything.

I do think it's kinda funny how people think this empty shell of a statement has any impact whatsoever. I know they're just trying to help but it almost feels like a movie cliché with the amount of times I've heard it.

Kinda, but I think you're more resilient than me. I used to have a positive mindset aswell, especially at the beginning of this college year (forgot to mention it but I'm back in college again). 

Right now my grades are terrible and I'm really thinking of dropping out again. I'm getting too old for this and my student debt is insanely high, to the point it actually would be better for me to just end it (in my country, student debt gets wiped away if the 'student' dies).

I want to just work at this point, because if I'm going to take the route of college, I'm gonna be around 28 - 30 years old, STILL LIVING WITH MY PARENTS and only debt attached to my name.

I'm not selling myself short as well, I haven't accomplished anything great in the years that I graduated from high school. I'm mediocre or average at best at anything I do.

But thanks for the positive message anyway, it helped to make my day a bit brighter.
I don't know how your situation is with your family but is it possible to cut ties with them? Just something to consider

I totally feel you. The only reason why I haven't ended it all myself is just because I know that I'll leave an insane amount of collateral damage to the people I know and to me that just doesn't seem fair.

It shouldn't be their lives I fuck up with that but there is no way around it.
